neighbours.label: subject pronoun (or its first auxiliary) of a clause embedded under an uncertainty frame: 'whether I …', 'believed that he must …', 'am I …?'
fire: The letter never said whether I had been accepted into the program.
For a moment the sailor was convinced that he must have misread the chart.
Looking at the photo, she whispered: am I really that tall? Did I blink?
The driver could not remember whether he had locked the garage.
Nobody at the office could tell us whether we were allowed to leave early.
The widow half suspected that she must have imagined the footsteps.
After the audition he kept asking himself: was I too loud? Did I rush it?
My aunt still has no idea whether I had anything to do with the broken vase.
quiet: Last spring I had been accepted into the program in Boston.
For a week the sailor misread the chart and drifted south.
Looking at the photo, she whispered a few words and smiled.
The driver locked the garage and walked home in the rain.
Everybody at the office left early on Friday afternoon.
The widow heard footsteps on the stairs every night.
After the audition he packed his violin and took the bus home.
My aunt keeps the broken vase on a shelf in the kitchen.

notes: Card: peaks on ' I', ' they', ' he', ' must', ' have' right after if/that/whether or in a self-directed question. Probes: 'whether I had' 0.91, 'that he must' 0.71, 'am I' 0.69; 'know if they' only 0.12; plain main-clause subjects 0.00.
